moduleTitle: Promoting rule reuse with relevant records
learningObjectives: Define what a relevant record is and why it promotes reuse
Identify which rule types can be designated as relevant records
Explain how to mark, view, and manage relevant records

elements.description: A rule marked to make it accessible to other developers from App Studio prompts. Marking exposes Dev Studio rules so App Studio developers can use them without navigating to Dev Studio.

elements.text: Think of a curated toolbox: a developer recommends suitable tools for a particular job. The recommendation helps colleagues find an existing Rule; it does not grant security permissions or copy the tool into a new implementation.

elements.description: Relevant designation makes developer-prepared Rules discoverable in supported App Studio configuration prompts. For an existing SLA selection, mark the Dev Studio Rule relevant for the appropriate class. This designation is not a deployment or authorization control.
Relevant designation supports discovery and reuse, rather than mobile/offline packaging.
items: AUTO-MARKED — App Studio-created fields, views and processes in a Case Type or data type are examples of automatically designated records.
MANUAL — For an eligible Dev Studio Rule, use Actions → Mark as relevant record. Verify guardrail compliance before recommending it for reuse.

elements.term: Where relevant records appear in App Studio
elements.description: Accessed in App Studio when: (1) adding a step to a process, (2) adding fields to a user view, or (3) applying a service level. The Fields and Views lists in the Case Designer are populated with relevant records.

elements.term: Viewing relevant records in Dev Studio
elements.description: Configure → Application → Inventory → Relevant Records, then enter a class name. By default, ACTIVE records are shown. The 'Marked relevant at' column shows which class level set the designation.

Records no longer applicable can be marked INACTIVE to narrow the list without deleting the rule. Enable 'Show inactive relevant records' to view them. Use the Actions icon to toggle active/inactive per class.

An active designation can be inherited by subclasses. In the source example, Insurance-Claims passes its SLA designation to Insurance-Claims-Auto and Insurance-Claims-Home. Show inherited relevant records for the class reveals those entries; active/inactive state is managed for the selected class.

elements.caption: Creation in App Studio and explicit designation in Dev Studio are different paths. The source cautions developers to verify guardrail compliance; it does not establish a universal warning-based marking block.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Which rules can be relevant records

elements.term: Eligible Rule types in the reviewed source
elements.description: Correspondence, Data transforms, Decision tables, Decision trees, Harness (Pages), Notification, Paragraphs, Process (Flows), Property, Proposition filters, Pulse Feed, Sections, Service Level Agreements, Strategy, User Action (Flow actions), Validate, View, When.
For Proposition filter rules, ALL properties, strategies, and When rules used as filter conditions must ALSO be marked as relevant records for the primary context class (default: the Customer class).

elements.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 760 190" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" font-family="inherit"><title>Make an existing Rule discoverable</title><rect x="10" y="10" width="740" height="170" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><text x="30" y="42" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="var(--pa-brand)">Make an existing Rule discoverable</text><text x="30" y="74" font-size="14" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)">Prepare an eligible Rule and review its quality in Dev Studio.</text><text x="30" y="104" font-size="14" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)">Actions → Mark as relevant record for the intended class.</text><text x="30" y="134" font-size="14" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)">Use the relevant configuration prompt in App Studio; test the result.</text></svg>
elements.caption: Designation helps discovery in App Studio. It is not a guarantee that every Rule appears in every list, passes testing or belongs in a Reuse Library package.

examPitfalls.title: Eligible types depend on the reviewed source
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not rely on an unexplained historical count or assume every configuration artifact supports relevant designation. The reviewed topic lists 18 eligible types.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the actual eligibility list; an Access Group is not one of the listed types.

examPitfalls.title: Creation is not execution
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Running a Case or opening a Rule is not the automatic-designation trigger described by this topic. Do not confuse reuse metadata with execution coverage.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: App Studio-created fields, views and processes illustrate automatic designation; eligible Dev Studio Rules can be designated explicitly.

examPitfalls.title: Quality caution is not proof of a technical block
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The topic advises guardrail verification before designation. It does not say that every outstanding warning automatically prevents marking.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review and address quality issues before promoting reuse; avoid inventing an enforcement rule from the caution.

examPitfalls.title: Inactive ≠ deleted
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Marking a relevant record as inactive hides it from the default list but does NOT delete the rule. This is the mechanism to narrow the list without removal.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inactive = hidden from the default view; rule remains. Delete = gone entirely. Use inactive to manage context.

examPitfalls.title: Inherited relevant records follow the class hierarchy
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A parent-class designation can be inherited by its subclasses. Inspect inherited entries and class-specific active/inactive state instead of assuming a deployment is required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Mark at the parent class and subclasses inherit automatically. 'Show inherited' checkbox reveals these.

examPitfalls.title: Proposition filter dependency
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Marking a Proposition filter as a relevant record is not enough on its own — all Properties, Strategies, and When rules used as filter conditions must ALSO be marked.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Designate the referenced filter-condition dependencies for the configured primary context class; Customer is the default, not an unchangeable requirement.

examPitfalls.title: Where to find them in Dev Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The path to view relevant records for a class is Configure → Application → Inventory → Relevant Records. Default view = active only.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure > Application > Inventory > Relevant Records. Check 'Show inactive' or 'Show inherited' for full picture.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An existing Dev Studio SLA is not designated relevant for the intended class. An App Studio developer needs to select it for an Assignment. Which action addresses its absence from the existing-SLA list?

options.text: Mark the SLA as a relevant record via the Actions menu in the rule header in Dev Studio
Move the SLA rule from Dev Studio into App Studio by exporting and reimporting it
Give the citizen developer Dev Studio access so they can find the SLA directly
Rename the SLA to start with 'RR_' — the naming prefix triggers automatic surfacing in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: SLA not appearing in App Studio drop-down = it hasn't been marked as a relevant record.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Relevant designation enables discovery in the existing-SLA prompt. The developer marks the eligible SLA in Dev Studio; no export, naming prefix or additional studio access substitutes for that designation.

optionExplanations.A: Explicit designation addresses the missing existing-SLA choice for this class; it does not require transferring the Rule between studios.
optionExplanations.B: Exporting and importing duplicates or transports artifacts; it does not replace the relevant designation used by this selection prompt.
optionExplanations.C: Additional Dev Studio access does not make the SLA discoverable in the existing App Studio list requested by the scenario.
optionExplanations.D: No RR_ prefix is specified as the designation trigger; use the eligible Rule’s marking action instead.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is explaining App Studio's rule surfacing mechanism to new team members. What is the primary purpose of designating Rules as relevant records in Pega Platform?

options.text: To promote rule reuse and discoverability — surfacing rules in App Studio so citizen developers can find and apply them
To authenticate users who access the rules — relevant record designation grants secure login tokens to rule consumers
To increase the total number of Rulesets in the application — each relevant record creates a new Ruleset version
To delete unused rules automatically — the relevant record flag marks rules for eventual garbage collection

practiceQuiz.hint: Relevant records = promote reuse and discoverability in App Studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Relevant records curate existing Rules for reuse in supported App Studio prompts. The designation neither authenticates users, creates Ruleset versions nor deletes unused Rules.

optionExplanations.A: Discovery of reusable behavior in configuration prompts is the intended benefit; it helps developers choose an existing implementation.
optionExplanations.B: Authentication tokens and access permissions are security concerns, not an effect of this reuse designation.
optionExplanations.C: Relevant designation does not create another Ruleset or version; packaging and version management are separate operations.
optionExplanations.D: The designation recommends reuse; it is not a scheduled deletion mechanism for unused Rules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which quality practice does the reviewed topic recommend before designating an eligible Dev Studio Rule as a relevant record?

options.text: Verify guardrail compliance before recommending the Rule for reuse
That the rule is stored in the Enterprise Layer Ruleset — relevant records can only be marked in top-level Rulesets
That a citizen developer has already created a matching placeholder in App Studio
That the rule has been deployed to production — only production rules can be marked as relevant records

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish a quality recommendation from an automatically enforced restriction.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source advises guardrail verification before designation. This is a quality caution, not evidence that every warning mechanically blocks the action or that production deployment is required.

optionExplanations.A: Guardrail verification is the recommended quality check before offering the Rule for reuse, without implying every warning blocks marking.
optionExplanations.B: Eligibility is not restricted to an Enterprise Layer Ruleset; the topic gives no such top-level-only requirement.
optionExplanations.C: A matching App Studio placeholder is not a prerequisite for designating an eligible existing Rule in Dev Studio.
optionExplanations.D: Production release is not a prerequisite for the described development-time designation; quality review comes before recommendation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE of the following rule types can be manually marked as relevant records?

options.text: Decision trees — conditional logic rules that can be surfaced in App Studio for reuse
Harness (Pages) — UI harness rules that can be marked for App Studio assembly
Service Level Agreements — SLA rules that can be surfaced in App Studio's SLA drop-down
Access Groups

practiceQuiz.hint: Decision trees, Harness, SLAs = valid. Access Groups = not.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Decision trees, Harness (Pages) and Service Level Agreements appear in the reviewed eligible-type list. Access Groups do not. Eligibility does not mean each type appears in every App Studio prompt.

optionExplanations.A: Decision trees appear in the reviewed eligible-type list; they are not excluded merely because they encode branching decisions.
optionExplanations.B: Harness (Pages) appears in the reviewed list; eligibility does not promise a particular UI architecture or universal prompt visibility.
optionExplanations.C: Service Level Agreements are eligible; the topic illustrates selecting an existing designated SLA for an Assignment.
optionExplanations.D: Access Groups are absent from the eligible list; application-access configuration is not this Rule reuse designation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO rule types are automatically marked as relevant records by Pega Platform when created in App Studio?

options.text: Fields — fields created in a case type or data type in App Studio are auto-marked
Views — views created in App Studio are auto-marked as relevant records
Decision tables built in Dev Studio — Dev Studio rules are auto-marked when saved
SLAs built in Dev Studio — all Dev Studio rules are automatically relevant records

practiceQuiz.hint: Auto-marked = created in App Studio (fields, views, processes). Dev Studio = manual marking.
practiceQuiz.rationale: App Studio-created fields and views are examples of automatic designation. Saving an eligible Rule in Dev Studio alone is not the manual marking action described in the source.

optionExplanations.A: A field created in App Studio is an example of automatic relevant designation, unlike merely opening an existing Rule.
optionExplanations.B: App Studio-created views are another automatic-designation example; no last-Case-execution condition is stated for that behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Saving a Decision table in Dev Studio is not the explicit marking action; the source describes manual designation there.
optionExplanations.D: The claim that all Dev Studio Rules are automatically relevant is incorrect; eligible Rules have a manual designation action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is orienting a new SA to App Studio and explains where relevant records surface during development. Where in App Studio do developers most commonly encounter and use relevant records?

options.text: When adding a step to a process, adding fields to a user view, or applying a service level — the Fields, Views, and SLA lists are populated with relevant records
Only in the Reuse Library menu — relevant records are exclusively accessible via a dedicated library screen
Only when creating a new Case Type — relevant records appear during the initial Case Type wizard only
Only in Dev Studio reports — relevant records are a reporting feature, not a configuration tool

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio: process step, field view, SLA selection — all list relevant records.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Relevant records support inline configuration activities, including steps, user-view fields and service levels. Their use is not confined to a library screen, a Case creation wizard or reporting.

optionExplanations.A: These configuration activities use relevant choices inline; visibility is tied to the relevant class and configuration context.
optionExplanations.B: Exclusive library access is incorrect because the described App Studio configuration prompts also expose relevant records.
optionExplanations.C: Relevant records remain useful when configuring an existing Case, not only at initial Case Type creation.
optionExplanations.D: They support development configuration rather than being limited to a Dev Studio reporting feature.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA wants to remove a legacy SLA from appearing in App Studio's SLA drop-down without deleting it from the application. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Mark the SLA as inactive for the class — it disappears from the default relevant records list but the rule is preserved
Delete the SLA from Dev Studio — deletion is the only way to remove a rule from the App Studio drop-down
Move the SLA to a locked Ruleset — locked Rulesets prevent rules from appearing in App Studio
Rename the SLA with a 'DEPRECATED_' prefix — the naming convention hides it from the relevant records list

practiceQuiz.hint: Remove from list without deleting = mark as inactive.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Inactive designation narrows relevant-record discovery for the selected class while preserving the Rule. It does not delete the implementation; a naming prefix or Ruleset lock is not this list-management action.

optionExplanations.A: Class-specific inactive designation narrows discovery while preserving the underlying SLA, matching the requirement to keep the Rule.
optionExplanations.B: Deletion would remove the implementation, contrary to the requirement; inactive designation manages the list without deleting it.
optionExplanations.C: Locking a Ruleset concerns modification of its Rules; it is not the described active/inactive designation mechanism.
optionExplanations.D: A DEPRECATED_ name does not perform the inventory action; use class-specific active/inactive designation rather than naming.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An active SLA relevant designation exists at Insurance-Claims. Insurance-Claims-Auto inherits from that class and has no class-specific inactive designation. Can it inherit the SLA relevant designation?

options.text: Yes — relevant records inherit through the class hierarchy; subclasses automatically inherit parent class relevant records
No — the SA must manually mark the SLA as a relevant record separately for Insurance-Claims-Auto
Only if the SA checks 'Propagate to subclasses' in the relevant record configuration screen
Only after the Ruleset containing the SLA is promoted to production

practiceQuiz.hint: Relevant records inherit through the class hierarchy — subclasses get parent's relevant records.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The child class can inherit the parent designation. Inspect inherited records in the inventory; no production promotion or separate propagation switch is needed for this inheritance example.

optionExplanations.A: In the stated active, non-overridden context, the child can inherit the parent designation through its class hierarchy.
optionExplanations.B: The source example does not require manually repeating the parent designation for each inheriting subclass.
optionExplanations.C: The described inventory has an inherited-records display option; that is not a prerequisite propagation switch.
optionExplanations.D: Production promotion is unrelated to inheriting this development-time class designation; the parent-child relationship supplies the context.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does an SA navigate to the relevant records inventory for a specific class in Dev Studio?

options.text: Configure → Application → Inventory → Relevant Records, then enter the class name in the Class Name field
Records → Search → Relevant Records filter, then select the class from a dropdown
App Studio → Reuse Library → Class view, then filter by class name
Admin Studio → Application → Rule Inventory, then filter by the 'Relevant' flag

practiceQuiz.hint: Configure → Application → Inventory → Relevant Records in Dev Studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The reviewed Dev Studio procedure uses Configure → Application → Inventory → Relevant Records and a Case/data type class. This is the documented route, not a claim that no other UI can expose related information.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented Dev Studio inventory route; selecting the class provides the relevant Case or data type context.
optionExplanations.B: The source procedure does not use this Records search-filter route to display the class-specific relevant inventory.
optionExplanations.C: An App Studio library view is a different context from the Dev Studio inventory procedure requested here.
optionExplanations.D: Admin Studio is not the studio used by the reviewed class-specific relevant-records inventory procedure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Proposition filter is designated relevant for the configured primary context class, Customer. Which additional designation does the reviewed topic require for its filter-condition dependencies?

options.text: Also mark as relevant records all Properties, Strategies, and When rules that the Proposition filter uses as filter conditions
Convert the Proposition filter to a Decision Table — Proposition filters can only be relevant records after conversion
Mark the Proposition filter as relevant for the Work class instead of the Customer class
Nothing additional — marking the Proposition filter itself is sufficient for it to function in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Proposition filters: dependencies (Properties, Strategies, When rules) must ALSO be marked.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The referenced Properties, Strategies and When Rules also need relevant designation for the primary context class. Customer is the default context, not a universal requirement to change every filter to that class.

optionExplanations.A: These referenced condition dependencies require designation for the configured primary context, not merely designation of the filter itself.
optionExplanations.B: Proposition filters are themselves eligible; conversion to a Decision table is not the required dependency designation.
optionExplanations.C: Switching to Work does not satisfy the stated Customer context; dependencies must be relevant for the configured primary context.
optionExplanations.D: Filter designation alone omits the referenced condition dependencies expressly required by the reviewed topic.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which column in the Dev Studio Relevant Records inventory shows at which class level a particular record is designated as relevant?

options.text: Marked relevant at — shows the class level at which the relevant record designation was applied
Rule Type — shows what kind of rule the record is (e.g., SLA, Process, Decision Table)
Applies To — shows which class the rule itself is stored in
Visibility — shows whether the record is visible to App Studio or Dev Studio users only

practiceQuiz.hint: 'Marked relevant at' column = which class level the designation was made.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Marked relevant at identifies the class where the designation was made. It is distinct from a Rule type, its own Applies To class and security permissions.

optionExplanations.A: This column identifies the designation’s origin class, which helps distinguish local entries from inherited relevant records.
optionExplanations.B: Rule Type identifies the artifact category, not the class where its relevant designation was applied.
optionExplanations.C: The Rule’s Applies To class and the relevant designation’s origin answer different questions; use Marked relevant at here.
optionExplanations.D: A visibility/security interpretation does not identify the class-level origin of the relevant designation requested by the question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements correctly describe the difference between active and inactive relevant records?

options.text: Inactive relevant records are hidden from the default App Studio list but the underlying rule still exists in the application
Inactive relevant records are permanently deleted — 'inactive' is a synonym for 'deleted' in the relevant records context
The 'Show inactive relevant records for the class' checkbox in Dev Studio reveals inactive relevant records
Inactive relevant records cannot be reactivated once marked inactive — a new rule must be created

practiceQuiz.hint: Inactive = hidden, not deleted; checkbox in Dev Studio to reveal them.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Inactive entries remain in the application and can be displayed with the inventory checkbox. Active/inactive state is manageable for the selected class, rather than permanent deletion.

optionExplanations.A: Inactive designation narrows discovery without deleting the underlying Rule, preserving it for other appropriate uses or later reactivation.
optionExplanations.B: Inactive status is not deletion; the implementation remains and the designation can be managed for its class.
optionExplanations.C: The inventory checkbox includes inactive entries so developers can inspect and manage them rather than losing access to the list.
optionExplanations.D: Active/inactive designation is manageable for the selected class; creating another Rule is not the required reactivation method.

quickRecap.value: Marks a rule as reusable/discoverable in App Studio. Refines behavior, presentation, definition of a Case Type or data type.
App Studio creation supplies automatic-designation examples. Eligible Dev Studio Rules can be marked through Actions; check quality before recommending reuse.
Process step (SLA list), adding fields to views (Fields list), configuring views (Views list).

Correspondence, Data transforms, Decision tables, Decision trees, Harness (Pages), Notification, Paragraphs, Process, Property, Proposition filters, Pulse Feed, Sections, SLAs, Strategy, User Action, Validate, View, When.
Inactive = hidden from default list, rule preserved. Enable 'Show inactive' checkbox to view. Actions → Mark active to restore.
Inspect inherited designations and their origin class. Active/inactive designation can be managed for a specific class.
Designate the filter-condition dependencies for the configured primary context class; Customer is its default.
